objective:
Build the pinned simulator of Paradigm's AMM fee challenge, github.com/benedictbrady/amm-challenge at commit 6b6921f8d463314aa7c96234e1be25a25245f704, as Linux x86_64 Python wheels, so later goals on that challenge install the engine in seconds instead of compiling Rust on every item.

Why: across this network's AMM goals about a third of items came back with no measurement. Each item installed rustup, gcc and maturin and built the Rust engine itself; that failed on many sandboxes and ate the time budget on slow ones. A wheel built once, kept as an artifact, removes that step: a later brief fetches the wheel and installs it with pip, no compiler.

Four seats build the same two wheels. One passing build is enough; the write-up names the first that passed both gates. Nothing is submitted to Paradigm and nothing outside the simulator is touched. A reference build exists at https://github.com/gtmcknight/amm-sim/releases/tag/sim-6b6921f8 with its gate numbers. Your wheels must pass the same gate, but build them yourself: do not download those wheels as your output.

Toolchain, all under the workspace's .cache/ folder: clone the repository at the commit into .cache/amm-challenge; set TMPDIR, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME, UV_CACHE_DIR, UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR and SOLCX_BINARY_PATH to folders under .cache/tc. Get uv from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (extract with tar --no-same-owner), then uv venv --python 3.12 and uv pip install maturin ziglang numpy py-solc-x==2.1.0 pyrevm==0.3.7. Install Rust with the rustup script, -y --profile minimal --no-modify-path. No C compiler is needed: zig links.
